references.text: Describes the process of embalming in Egypt, as Jacob was embalmed – the same procedure Joseph underwent.
Moses took Joseph's bones out of Egypt, fulfilling the oath the Israelites had sworn to Joseph.
Mentions Joseph's faith – that at his death he spoke of the Israelites' exodus from Egypt and gave instructions concerning his bones.
Joseph speaks of God's promise and asks his brothers to take his bones with them when God leads them out of Egypt.
Joseph's bones were eventually buried in Shechem, fulfilling his wish expressed before his death.
Parallel summary of the patriarchs' lifespans and deaths in Egypt, marking the end of the first generation of the family in exile.
Continues the story of Joseph's life in Egypt from his father's burial to his own death and coffin.
Creates a narrative framework spanning from Joseph's entry into Egypt to his death there.
Parallel treatment of Jacob and Joseph through embalming as a sign of honor in Egypt.
Theological parallel between two great leaders who died at the age of 110, marking respectively the end of exile and the beginning of the conquest.
Fulfillment of Jacob's deathbed promise: Joseph honors his father's wish not to be buried permanently in Egypt.
The contrast between Joseph's forced arrival in Egypt (as a slave) and his death there (as an honored leader).
New Testament allusion confirming that Joseph's journey to Egypt (sold by his brothers) was under God's guidance.
